Output power is low on every channel, and, since the noise added is unchanged, the signal-to-noise ratio of every channel falls too. This is a gradual or step degradation rather than an outage. About 1 per cent of units per year.

con.the_signal_to_noise_ratio_falls.label: the signal-to-noise ratio falls
con.the_signal_to_noise_ratio_falls.gloss: A symptom of the fault 'Gain loss': The unit's gain falls below its set point. Output power is low on every channel, and, since the noise added is unchanged, the signal-to-noise ratio of every channel falls too. This is a gradual or step degradation rather than an outage. About 1 per cent of units per year.

Traffic is unaffected until the drive current reaches its limit; the trend gives early warning and leads eventually to the end-of-life alarm (AMP_PUMP_EOL). This is a slow, incipient condition. About 2 per cent of units per year.

con.traffic_is_unaffected_until_the_driv.label: Traffic is unaffected until the drive current reaches its limit

Traffic is unaffected until the drive current reaches its limit; the trend gives early warning and leads eventually to the end-of-life alarm (AMP_PUMP_EOL). This is a slow, incipient condition. About 2 per cent of units per year.

con.gives_early_warning.label: gives early warning
con.gives_early_warning.gloss: A symptom of the fault 'Pump ageing': As the pump laser ages, the unit raises its drive current to hold the gain. Traffic is unaffected until the drive current reaches its limit; the trend gives early warning and leads eventually to the end-of-life alarm (AMP_PUMP_EOL). This is a slow, incipient condition. About 2 per cent of units per year.

con.leads_eventually_to_the_end_of_life_.gloss: A symptom of the fault 'Pump ageing': As the pump laser ages, the unit raises its drive current to hold the gain. Traffic is unaffected until the drive current reaches its limit; the trend gives early warning and leads eventually to the end-of-life alarm (AMP_PUMP_EOL). This is a slow, incipient condition. About 2 per cent of units per year.

loc.the_fibre_section_feeding_this_unit.label: the fibre section feeding this unit
loc.the_fibre_section_feeding_this_unit.gloss: Where the probable cause 'the fibre section feeding this unit is broken' of alarm AMP_INPUT_LOS lies, relative to the unit raising the alarm.
loc.the_fibre_section_feeding_this_unit.example: when no light arrives at its input

loc.the_preceding_amplifier.label: the preceding amplifier
loc.the_preceding_amplifier.gloss: Where the probable cause 'the preceding amplifier has failed and emits no light' of alarm AMP_INPUT_LOS lies, relative to the unit raising the alarm.
loc.the_preceding_amplifier.example: when no light arrives at its input

loc.at_the_input_of_the_multiplex_sectio.label: at the input of the multiplex section
loc.at_the_input_of_the_multiplex_sectio.gloss: Where the probable cause 'the patch cord may have been disconnected' of alarm OMS_LOS_P lies, relative to the unit raising the alarm.
loc.at_the_input_of_the_multiplex_sectio.example: when no light arrives at the input of the receiving end of the multiplex section

loc.the_fibre_section_feeding_the_unit_n.label: the fibre section feeding the unit, not against the unit itself
loc.the_fibre_section_feeding_the_unit_n.gloss: What alarm OSC_LOS is reported against.

loc.through_the_switch.label: through the switch
loc.through_the_switch.gloss: Where the symptom 'is interrupted' of 'Switch fabric failure' shows, relative to the faulty unit.
loc.through_the_switch.example: Every ODU cross-connected through the switch is interrupted: an alarm indication signal is carried onwards on each.

loc.the_wrong_destination.label: the wrong destination
loc.the_wrong_destination.gloss: Where the symptom 'is delivered to the wrong destination' of 'Wrong cross-connection' shows, relative to the faulty unit.
loc.the_wrong_destination.example: A cross-connection has been provisioned wrongly, so one ODU is delivered to the wrong destination. There is no optical symptom.

loc.on_the_odu_path_currently_in_use.label: on the ODU path currently in use
loc.on_the_odu_path_currently_in_use.gloss: Where the probable cause 'any failure' of alarm CLIENT_SF lies, relative to the unit raising the alarm.

loc.at_either_end.label: at either end
loc.at_either_end.gloss: Where the probable cause 'a failure of the client port' of alarm CLIENT_SF lies, relative to the unit raising the alarm.

loc.in_an_otn_switch_along_the_odu_path.label: in an OTN switch along the ODU path
loc.in_an_otn_switch_along_the_odu_path.gloss: Where the probable cause 'a wrong cross-connection' of alarm CLIENT_SF lies, relative to the unit raising the alarm.

loc.client_port.label: client port
loc.client_port.gloss: What alarm CLIENT_SF is reported against.

loc.on_the_working_odu_path.label: on the working ODU path
loc.on_the_working_odu_path.gloss: Where the probable cause 'any failure' of alarm PROT_ACTIVE lies, relative to the unit raising the alarm.
loc.on_the_working_odu_path.example: The selector is on the protection path.

loc.on_the_protection_odu_path.label: on the protection ODU path
loc.on_the_protection_odu_path.gloss: Where the probable cause 'any failure' of alarm PROT_UNAVAIL lies, relative to the unit raising the alarm.

loc.this_port.label: this port
loc.this_port.gloss: Where the probable cause 'failure' of alarm EQPT_PORT_FAIL lies, relative to the unit raising the alarm.

loc.this_switch_s_fabric.label: this switch's fabric
loc.this_switch_s_fabric.gloss: Where the probable cause 'failure' of alarm OTN_FABRIC_FAIL lies, relative to the unit raising the alarm.

loc.otn_switch.label: OTN switch
loc.otn_switch.gloss: What alarm OTN_FABRIC_FAIL is reported against.

sev.critical.label: critical
sev.critical.example: No light at the line receiver.

sev.minor.label: minor
sev.minor.example: the margin falls below about 1 dB

sev.not_alarmed.label: not alarmed
sev.not_alarmed.example: The far end reports a defect on the signal this unit transmits.

sev.major.label: major
sev.major.example: when the supervisory channel is not received

correspondences.rationale: Both denote a ROADM network unit; the VB concept identifies the vendor-specific implementation of the shared ROADM resource.
The VB transponder is the vendor-specific coherent line-interface kind identified as transponder in model B.
Both denote the muxponder kind of coherent line interface.
Model B explicitly defines otn_line as the OTN line-card kind represented by the VB unit.
Both denote the amplifier role or position at the transmitting end of an optical multiplex section.
Both denote the inline-amplifier role at intermediate amplifier sites.
Both denote the preamplifier role or position at the receiving end of an optical multiplex section.
Both denote an OTN switching unit providing ODU cross-connect functionality.
Both denote the generic client-port resource, independent of a particular Ethernet rate.
Both denote per-channel optical power reported by an optical channel monitor.
Both denote per-channel OSNR reported by an optical channel monitor.
Both denote received-power performance-counter measurements; B explicitly identifies the 15-minute binning that is implicit in the performance-counter context of A.
Both denote line errored seconds accumulated in 15-minute performance-monitoring bins.
A explicitly describes optical power at the line receiver, exactly matching B's receiver optical power.
Both denote OSNR estimated by coherent receiver DSP monitoring.
BER is the standard abbreviation for bit error ratio; both specify the pre-FEC coherent-receiver measurement.
DGD is the standard abbreviation for differential group delay, and both are coherent DSP measurements.
Both denote the DSP-estimated rate of change of optical state of polarisation.
Both denote total optical power at the monitored amplifier/unit input.
Both denote total optical power at the monitored amplifier/unit output.
Both denote amplifier pump drive current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value.
Both denote a monitor, exemplified by an OSC receiver, that raises alarms but does not report measured values.
Both denote client errored-seconds performance monitoring; B makes the customary 15-minute binning explicit.
Both denote client unavailable-seconds performance monitoring; B makes the customary 15-minute binning explicit.
Both denote availability of optical channel monitoring when the channel-monitoring capability is installed.
Both denote standard monitoring available on every unit, including performance counters.
Both denote optical received-power monitoring available on units fitted with the power-monitoring option.
Both denote advanced coherent-DSP monitoring available with the advanced monitoring capability.
Both denote absence of detectable optical signal at the line receiver.
Both denote reduced optical power on a signal or channel.
Both denote loss of reception of the optical supervisory channel.
Both denote degradation of optical signal-to-noise ratio.
A polarization change faster than receiver tracking is the fast state-of-polarization change denoted by POL_TRANSIENT.
The A condition is reduced signal quality caused by a shifted or narrowed WSS passband, matching the spectral narrowing or misalignment penalty in B.
Both denote failure of the unit itself, with traffic and valid operation lost.
Both denote loss of OTU frame alignment at a line receiver.
Both denote pre-FEC errors exceeding the degradation threshold while the signal remains framed.
Both denote an ODU alarm indication signal propagated downstream on an ODU path.
Both denote an ODU delivered to the wrong destination by a cross-connect.
Both denote failure or interruption of the client service.
Both denote a brief client-service interruption during a protection switch.
Both denote the characteristic pump-ageing condition in which drive current rises to maintain gain.
Both denote independent per-channel switching, with conditions following each separately routed channel.
Carrying the ODU alarm indication signal onward through each cross-connection is passing the arriving condition through unchanged.
Both denote a per-channel WSS attenuation deviation from its configured value.
Both denote frequency displacement or misalignment of a WSS channel passband.
Both denote hard failure of a WSS port; model A specializes it to an input port.
Both denote failure or loss of output from a transponder transmit laser.
Both denote a hard card failure.
Both denote degradation of a coherent receiver that impairs signal quality without necessarily removing light.
Both denote a broken or cut fibre that prevents light from passing.
Both denote disconnection of a connector or patch cord.
Both denote increased optical loss in a fibre span or section.
A rise in amplifier-added noise corresponds to an increase in the amplifier noise figure.
Both denote an increase in differential group delay on the fibre path.
Both denote a rapid transient change in optical state of polarisation.
Both denote connector contamination that adds optical loss.
Both are generic placeholders for any failure on the path toward the far end.
Both denote failure of an amplifier pump laser or amplifier unit resulting in no output.
Both denote amplifier gain falling below its set point.
Both denote ageing of an amplifier pump manifested by increasing pump drive current.
Both denote amplifier gain becoming non-flat across the optical band.
Both denote hard failure of an OTN switch fabric affecting cross-connected ODUs.
Both denote an incorrectly provisioned OTN cross-connect delivering an ODU to the wrong destination.
Both denote failure of a client port or its optical interface.
Both denote a non-outage degradation in which service continues with reduced quality.
A failed WSS input port is a hard failure and is consistent with the shared category of abrupt traffic loss.
The concept explicitly denotes degradation rather than outage, matching the definition of soft.
Gain loss reduces output quality and signal-to-noise ratio without constituting an outage, which is a soft fault.
Both denote a slow developing trend that provides warning before failure while traffic remains unaffected.
Gain tilt impairs some channels without causing an outage, directly matching the soft degradation category.
The WSS attenuation drift affects one optical channel.
The shifted or narrowed WSS passband pertains to one optical channel.
Both denote all channels arriving on one ROADM degree's input port.
The failed transmit laser causes loss of one optical channel.
This is the single optical channel transmitted by the failed card.
Both explicitly restrict the scope to this receiver alone.
The channels other than the receiver's affected channel form a non-total subset of the multiplex.
Both denote the equipment unit itself rather than a set of carried traffic.
Every channel carried by the failed unit is the entire multiplexed channel set at that unit.
Both denote every channel in the multiplexed signal.
In the amplifier context, unaffected traffic comprises all multiplexed channels carried by the unit.
Band-edge channels are the canonical example of some, but not all, multiplexed channels.
The meanings are explicitly identical: some channels, not all.
Both denote every ODU cross-connected through the switch.
In context, 'each' refers distributively to every ODU cross-connected through the switch.
Both denote a single ODU.
Both denote the particular client service affected by the client-port failure.
Both denote the local unit against which the alarm is raised.
Both denote the local port that raised or is associated with the alarm.
The fibre section feeding the unit is the immediately preceding upstream fibre span.
Both denote the amplifier immediately upstream of the unit.
Both denote the input connection of the optical multiplex section.
In the OCH_LOS context, a break along the incoming channel path is a failure somewhere upstream on that path.
Both denote the remote transmitting line interface feeding the local receiver.
Both denote the remote receiver that receives the signal transmitted by the local side.
Both denote the network path between the local unit and the far-end line interface, despite a directional wording difference.
In context, 'either end' means either client-service endpoint port.
Both denote an OTN switch or cross-connect situated on the service's ODU path.
Both denote the working ODU path and the resources on which it depends.
Both denote the protection ODU path and the resources on which it depends.
Both denote whichever ODU path is currently carrying the service.
Both denote the critical alarm severity.
Both denote the minor alarm severity.
Both denote a reported condition that is not alarmed.
Both denote the major alarm severity.
